Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509

Class X509TlsConnectorCustomizer

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509.X509TlsConnectorCustomizer
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.boot.web.server.WebServerFactoryCustomizer<org.springframework.boot.tomcat.servlet.TomcatServletWebServerFactory>
public class X509TlsConnectorCustomizer extends Object implements org.springframework.boot.web.server.WebServerFactoryCustomizer<org.springframework.boot.tomcat.servlet.TomcatServletWebServerFactory>
Adds the dedicated TLS port that requests a client certificate, when authserver.x509.port is set. The main port is left as it is, so the rest of the application never asks a browser for a certificate. The connector requests a certificate without requiring one and without validating it against a CA (optionalNoCA): the TLS handshake proves that the client holds the private key, and what identifies the client is the fingerprint of the certificate, which has to be bound to an account. The servlet container leaves the certificate in the request attribute that the X.509 filter reads. The connector's trust manager (AnyClientCertificateTrustManager) advertises no certificate authority: without it the handshake lists the authorities of the JVM's default trust store, and a client offers only a certificate issued by a listed authority, so the certificate of a private authority would never be presented.
